excerpt: const filename = `route-${routeId}.gpx`; const fullPath = path.join(exportDir, filename); fs.writeFileSync(fullPath, gpxData);
why: routeId is `z.string()` with no format restriction and is concatenated directly into the on-disk filename with no traversal check. path.join collapses '..' segments even when they are embedded inside a component that also has literal text (e.g. "route-" + "/../../tmp/pwned" -> "route-/../../tmp/pwned.gpx"), so a value like routeId="/../../../../etc/cron.d/pwned" makes fullPath resolve outside exportDir entirely (verified path.join's normalize behavior directly with node's built-in 'path' module, independent of this repo's code: path.join('/opt/exports','route-/../../../../../../../etc/cron.d/pwned.gpx') -> '/etc/cron.d/pwned.gpx'). The written content (gpxData) is fetched from Strava using the caller's own token, but the destination path is fully attacker-controlled, giving an arbitrary local file write (bounded only by the fixed '.gpx' suffix and process file permissions).
contract: Exports a specific Strava route in GPX format and saves it to a pre-configured local directory.

excerpt: const filename = `route-${routeId}.tcx`; const fullPath = path.join(exportDir, filename); fs.writeFileSync(fullPath, tcxData);
why: Identical pattern and bug to export-route-gpx (same file structure, same unsanitized routeId concatenation, same path.join traversal collapse), just writing the '.tcx' extension instead of '.gpx'. No validation rejects '/', '..', or absolute-path-like routeId values before the write.
contract: Exports a specific Strava route in TCX format and saves it to a pre-configured local directory.

tools/register-tools.js registerCreateProjectTool validates projectId is a non-empty string then calls lib/cloud-api/projects.js createProjectAndAttachBilling, which issues Cloud Resource Manager / Billing REST API calls with projectId as a JSON field; no shell or filesystem sink, only the caller's own GCP account is affected.

tools/register-tools.js registerDeployContainerImageTool forwards imageUrl to lib/deployment/deployer.js deployImage(), which only threads imageUrl into the Cloud Run Admin API service-creation request body (verified no exec/fs use of imageUrl in deployer.js); Cloud Run pulls the image server-side, this process never executes anything with imageUrl.

sink: child_process.exec() of a double-quoted shell string built by directly interpolating the caller-supplied folder path
why: tools/register-tools.js registerDeployLocalFolderTool only checks that folderPath is a non-empty string, then calls deploy({files:[folderPath],...}). Whenever the direct/no-Cloud-Build path is taken (deployWithZip, attempted first via deployer.js's canDeployWithoutBuild) or a docker-compose file is detected in the folder (deployCompose, which unconditionally calls prepareSourceDirectory), lib/deployment/source-processor.js's prepareSourceDirectory() runs `fsp.stat(file)`; if it is a directory it runs `execAsync(`cp -R "${file}/." "${tempDir}/"`)` via node:child_process exec, which spawns /bin/sh -c on the fully interpolated string. Because `file` is the raw folderPath with no escaping, any folder path containing a literal double-quote followed by shell syntax (e.g. a directory actually named `/tmp/x"; touch /tmp/pwned; echo "`) breaks out of the quoted argument and runs arbitrary shell commands with the privileges of the MCP server process. fs.stat/exec do not shell-parse the path themselves, so the only requirement for exploitation is that such a path exists on disk and is passed verbatim as folderPath -- the schema places no restriction on the string's shape. This is a real, unguarded shell-metacharacter injection, not just a robustness issue.
contract: Deploy a local folder to Cloud Run. Takes an absolute folder path from the local filesystem that will be deployed.

sink: used verbatim as the entry name inside a zip archive that is uploaded to a GCS bucket and later unpacked by Google Cloud Build / Cloud Run's buildpacks
why: tools/register-tools.js registerDeployFileContentsTool only checks that each file has non-empty content; the filename string (which the tool's own description says can be a path like 'src/index.js' or 'data/config.json') flows unmodified into archiver's archive.append({name: file.filename}) with no rejection of '..' segments or absolute paths, so a filename like '../../malicious' would be written into the zip under that literal traversal path. Whether this is exploitable depends entirely on how Google's Cloud Build / buildpacks source-extraction unpacks the archive server-side, which is outside this repo and cannot be inspected from source, so I cannot confirm a concrete bypass or rule one out -- this is a real, unguarded mechanism in this repo's own code but the impact is unproven, matching Tier B rather than Tier A.
contract: Deploy files to Cloud Run by providing their contents directly. Takes an array of file objects containing filename and content.

why: tools/register-tools.js registerGetServiceTool forwards project/region/service to lib/cloud-api/run.js getService(), which builds a Cloud Run Admin API resource name via runClient.servicePath(project, location, serviceId) (the client library's own path builder, not string concatenation into a URL or shell) and calls the gRPC getService RPC; only returns data about the caller's own project.

tools/register-tools.js registerGetServiceLogTool forwards project/region/service to lib/cloud-api/run.js getServiceLogs(), which builds a Cloud Logging filter string by directly interpolating serviceId/location without escaping (`resource.labels.service_name="${serviceId}"`). This is an unguarded filter-string injection in this repo's own code, but the loggingClient is already scoped to the caller-supplied `projectId`, and Cloud Logging IAM (roles/logging.viewer etc.) is granted at the project/bucket level, not per Cloud Run service -- so breaking out of the service_name/location clause only lets the query see logs the caller's own token can already read within that project by simply calling this same tool again with a different `service`/`region` argument. There is no confidentiality boundary the injection uniquely crosses, so it does not meet the 'genuine security property' bar for a finding.
tools/register-tools.js registerListProjectsTool has inputSchema: {} (no parameters); it calls listProjects(options.accessToken) with only the server's own configured access token.

tools/register-tools.js registerListServicesTool forwards only `project` (a string) to lib/cloud-api/run.js listServices(), which uses runClient.locationPath(projectId, location) (client-library path builder) per discovered location and calls the gRPC listServices RPC; only lists the caller's own project's services.
